Subject: PrivCP deployment — SAML / SCIM questions and metadata

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood's private control plane model earlier today. Acme is moving ahead with the VPC private deployment and we need to lock down the identity contract so our security and ops teams can proceed with the network cutover.

Two immediate asks:
1) Can you share a concise list of SAML attributes Redwood expects for operator vs app-level access? We have to map these to our existing AD groups and to the SecureID integrator.
2) For SCIM provisioning, which schema extensions does Redwood rely on (groups, entitlements, externalId usage)? We want to avoid a long back-and-forth.

Subject: Re: PrivCP deployment — SAML / SCIM questions and metadata

Tara,

Appreciate the metadata — that's perfect. High level answers up front:
- SAML attributes: we require a stable primary identifier (email or persistent uid), and one attribute to convey role/entitlement. Our recommended attribute name is "redwood_entitlements" (multi-valued) for role-based mapping, and we also accept standard Group membership via "groups".
- SCIM: we support core User and Group resources (RFC7643) and a small extension that carries "entitlements" and "externalId" on Groups. See the SCIM sample you should receive from Acme (or we can provide our sample).

I'll set up a 60-minute design sync with our infra + product folks tomorrow. In advance I've attached a rough mapping matrix (redwood-privcp-id-mapping-draft.xlsx) that maps Acme groups -> Redwood roles -> operator capabilities. Please pass that to your SRE and identity teams.

Action items proposed:
- Confirm primary nameID (email vs persistent uid)
- Agree on SAML signing algorithm / assertion expiry policy
- SCIM provisioning scope: full provisioning vs delta (we usually recommend delta pushes for groups)

Meeting: 2025-09-12 10:00 PT (calendar invite to follow).

Cheers,
Ben Carter

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2025-09-11T10:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivCP deployment — SAML / SCIM questions and metadata

Tara / Ben — quick product constraints to call out before the sync:
- Attribute contract: our control plane enforces an entitlement-based RBAC. We accept either a single multi-valued attribute ("redwood_entitlements") or SAML Group assertions. We do NOT rely on LDAP groups for run-time evaluation inside the customer's VPC — group -> role mapping is translated at the control plane during assertion ingestion.
- NameID: email is easiest for existing customers; persistent immutable ids are preferred for customers that perform reorganizations. If Acme can provide both (email + persistent externalId), that gives us the most robust mapping.
- Delegated admin: Operator-level access (deploy/scale/trace) must be tied to a scoped role (e.g., privcp_operator). We support short-lived session tokens derived from the SAML assertion; for unattended operator tooling we recommend service-account-style SCIM-provisioned users with an externalId and tightly-scoped permissions.

I want the team to agree on assertion lifetime: default 5 minutes is our baseline; we can accept up to 15 minutes for cross-region timings but we then require replay protection and assertion IDs recorded for 24h.

Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tara Jensen <tara.jensen@acmecorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-11T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivCP deployment — SAML / SCIM questions and metadata

Tara — couple of engineering clarifications so our infra team can prepare the SP config:
- Assertion signing alg: we accept RSA-SHA256. If your IdP signs with a different alg (eg. RSA-SHA1) we need the cert and to validate the compatibility early.
- ACS / Audience: we need your IdP to send assertions with Audience matching the SP EntityID we'll provide (I'll send the value in the invite).
- SP-initiated vs IdP-initiated: we support both. For operator UIs we recommend SP-initiated with RelayState preserved; for CI/service access we expect IdP-initiated flows mapped to SCIM-provisioned service users.
- Persistent session vs short-lived: code paths that call into the control plane programmatically should use token exchange (SAML -> short-lived API tokens).

Also, does Acme plan to push full group sync on initial cutover, or will you do a delta (add/remove) approach? Deltas are easier for us to reconcile with minimal disruption.

-- Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Tara Jensen <tara.jensen@acmecorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2025-09-12T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivCP deployment — SAML / SCIM questions and metadata

Thanks everyone — answers below and attaching a small SCIM sample export.
- NameID: we will supply email as NameID and include an "employeeId" attribute as a persistent external id.
- Signing alg: SecureID will sign with RSA-SHA256; attaching the certificate to the metadata.
- Initial provisioning: we'll do a full initial group dump to seed the mapping, then delta SCIM updates for day-to-day changes.
- Assertion expiry: 10 minutes works for our users.
- Operator accounts: we don't want human operator actions to use long-lived service accounts. We'll provision a small set of service users (SCIM) for automation and require MFA for human operator console access.

Attachments: acme-scim-sample.json (8 KB)

We also asked SecureID to stand up a test tenant. Integrations team is copied. Can Redwood provide a test SP URL and a sample assertion for us to validate?

-Tara
[Attachment: acme-scim-sample.json (JSON, 8 KB)]

- Attribute for role/entitlements = "redwood_entitlements" (multi-valued) + Group assertions accepted.
- Signing = RSA-SHA256; assertion expiry = 10 minutes; replay protection = ON in the control plane.
- Provisioning = full initial group export + delta SCIM updates thereafter. Service-users will be provisioned via SCIM with externalId and explicit "privcp_operator" role where needed.
